sections.h2: Selling a Mount Pleasant house without a long wait
sections.html:
Your choices are an agent, a sale on your own, or an outright cash purchase. Anyone with a half-finished repair, an estate still in probate or a move-out date that cannot slip may lean toward cash, since it ends the cycle of open houses and lender waits.

The village has 28,253 residents, and owners live in roughly 76.8 percent of its homes. Over 2020 to 2024 the median owner-occupied value was $292,400 and median household income was $91,616. About 22.0% of residents are 65 or older, so expect retirees among your likely buyers as well as families. The village counted 11,883 households for 2020 to 2024, averaging 2.33 people each.

Location helps your pitch. Mount Pleasant is about 30 miles south of Milwaukee and 60 miles north of Chicago and covers about 34 square miles. Mention the Milwaukee and Chicago drive times in your listing if commuters are your likely buyers.

sections.h2: What to tell buyers about development
sections.html: Big projects have put this village in the news. Foxconn announced a $10 billion display campus in October 2017, though the plan was scaled back later. In September 2025 Microsoft announced a large data center here. If a buyer wonders what is going up near your street, do not speculate. Refer that person to the village planning and engineering departments, which handle zoning and approvals for additions and new structures.

The Racine Unified School District runs the public schools, and Case High School, inside the village, takes almost every address. A few streets are zoned for Park High School in Racine. A school zone named in your listing spares buyers an extra errand.

The village handles permit applications through an online BS&A account that is free to open. Before listing, review these points.

  • New structures and qualifying remodeling or alterations need building permits, and additions also require zoning and engineering approval.
  • Work on one- and two-family houses falls under the Uniform Dwelling Code, and wiring under the National Electric Code and SPS 316.
  • Owners may pull their own permits after reading and signing a Cautionary Statement, while hired contractors must hold state dwelling contractor credentials.
  • The state Lead Safe Rules apply to renovation of any house built before 1978.

Phone an inspector on a weekday between 7:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m., or email buildinginspection@mtpleasantwi.gov. Previous owners sometimes added a deck, a finished basement or a garage with no permit. If that happened to you, call the department about closing the file before a buyer's inspector raises it.

Think of Wis. Stat. 709.02 as a ten-day homework assignment. Most sellers of one-to-four unit homes owe the buyer a finished condition report by day 10 after the contract is accepted. If it has not arrived, the buyer can cancel in the two business days that follow and take deposits back. Someone settling an estate may be off the hook, because a court-supervised fiduciary who never lived in the house is excused.

Wis. Stat. 77.22 assigns the transfer fee to the seller, at 30 cents per $100 of value. A few transfers escape it under section 77.25: those by will, those from parent to child for nominal consideration, and a foreclosure deed handed to the mortgage holder. When you claim one of these, the deed itself must carry the reason.

Your deed goes to the Racine County Register of Deeds, since the village lies in that county. Expect a flat $30 to record it. If a former co-owner has died, form HT-110 (termination of decedent's property interest) is also $30. The electronic transfer return is where the separate state fee gets calculated.

What a recordable document needs
RequirementDetail
PartiesGrantor and grantee named
SignatureGrantor signature notarized or authenticated
PropertyComplete legal description and parcel identification number
DrafterDrafter's name and a mailing address for the return
FormatLegible text that follows state margin and layout rules

The county office offers basic information and little else, so a title company or an attorney usually prepares and files the deed for you.

sections.h2: Tax bills and the closing split
sections.html:
Valuation day is January 1. Bills have to be mailed no later than the third Monday in December. Installment payers send half by January 31 and half by July 31. Pay the first half late and the whole bill becomes delinquent on February 1, accruing 1 percent interest a month.

Ask the village treasurer or the Racine County treasurer for a current statement on your parcel. The closing agent then allocates the year's tax between you and the buyer.

Putting the house on the market draws buyers with loans, along with showings, inspection requests and lender delays. Someone paying cash needs no lender and takes the house in its current state, which leaves title work and your calendar as the main limits on the closing date.

  • Get each offer on paper, naming the closing date and the party paying title and recording costs.
  • Compare offers by the amount left once your mortgage and any liens are paid.
  • Hand over copies of permit records and the condition report so both sides read the same facts.
  • Before you phone anyone, find the parcel number, your lender's name and any HOA or special assessment notices.

For a house in probate, tell the buyer at the start who may sign. Racine County will not record a deed without the right signatures and a notary's acknowledgment.

sections.h2: Village services a buyer may ask about
sections.html:
Buyers like to know who provides what. The village runs its own sanitary sewer and storm water utilities and buys its drinking water from the city of Racine. Fire and ambulance service comes from the South Shore Fire Department, and the village keeps its own police department. Building, planning, engineering and finance departments work in house, which means most permit and zoning questions can be settled with one village office rather than the county.

The village has had its own zoning ordinance since 1972, so land-use rules are set locally. A board of six trustees and an elected village president govern.

Accepting an offer starts the condition report clock. Use the 10 days well. Finish the report and answer every item. Dig up permit records for any deck, basement or garage work. Request a tax statement from the treasurer. Then ask the title company or attorney who is drafting the deed.

Next the transfer return is filed electronically, and the deed goes to the register. Once recorded, the sale becomes public record. A cash buyer saves you the lender's appraisal and the loan approval, but each step above still happens.

faqs.q: How many people live in Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: The village has 28,253 residents. The 2020 census count was 27,732.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Mount Pleasant?
faqs.a: The Racine Unified School District. Case High School serves almost all of the village, and a few areas are zoned to Park High School in Racine.

faqs.q: Can I pull my own building permit in the village?
faqs.a: Yes, after reading and signing the Cautionary Statement on the village's forms page. Contractors on one- and two-family homes need state dwelling contractor credentials.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Racine County?
faqs.a: Recording is a flat $30. If the sale is not exempt, the seller also owes the Wisconsin transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value.

faqs.q: Do estate sellers need to give a condition report?
faqs.a: Not when the personal representative or other court-supervised fiduciary never occupied the property, under Wis. Stat. 709.01. A seller who lived in the house must still complete it.
